STRATEGY: Parent is a conditional cooperator that retaliates to opponent defection and defects in the endgame; the trace simulates it against TFT, AllC, AllD, and periodic probes. The trace proposes probing with early defections, detecting retaliation vs non-retaliation, and switching to always-defect against non-retaliatory opponents.

It changes the parent by probing earlier and exploiting AllC more aggressively, while comparing scores against one_D_TFT, four_D_TFT, sustained_D, and periodic_D.

STRATEGY: The parent cooperates early, retaliates against frequent defection, uses TFT with forgiveness, and exploits in the endgame. The trace simulates candidate revisions (S, S1, S2, probe-based TFT variants) against periodic_D, AllC, TFT, one_D_TFT, four_D_TFT, four_D_ALLC, and sustained_D. It changes the parent by adding an early probe against perfect cooperators, continuing defection if no retaliation, and using a modified TFT rule that forgives single defections but retaliates after two consecutive defections.

Because we forgive too much, we cooperate against AllD and get 0. Parent defects more against AllD. We need to punish AllD harder."
STRATEGY: The parent uses a TFT-with-forgiveness strategy that cooperates early and retaliates to defections. The trace simulates the parent against four_D_ALLC, sustained_D, and periodic_D, then adds an AllD-detection rule (defect if opp_def_count == n) and an exploit mode (defect if my_def_count >= 2 and retaliation_count == 0). It then considers adopting a slot-3-like strategy that cooperates for 10 rounds before acting, and adds a probe against always-cooperators after 30 rounds of mutual cooperation.

The trace simulates it against one_D_TFT, four_D_TFT, four_D_ALLC, sustained_D, and periodic_D, then adds an early probe/exploit branch for opponents that never defect and a last-5-defections rule to detect always-defecting opponents.
